title: Detroit's dance halls and local club dates with his brother Gus
summary: Wilson describes Detroit bands, the Palais, and picking up weddings and club dates as teenagers; Gus played trombone and arranged.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: When I came to Chicago --and I have to lead into that, but coming out of Detroit, I met Roy Eldridge in Detroit, he was based there as a young fellow in those days, and oh, let's see, Milt Buckner was, I think he might have -- well, I don't even know if he was born yet, but his older brother, Ted, was around.

He was the lead alto player with Earl Walton's band at the Palais, one of the leading dance halls -- because the dance hall was a big outlet for musicians in those days, because everybody was dancing to our kind of music -- either jazz or some form of music, we called the sweet bands or the hot bands -- the jazz bands were the hot bands, so Billy Minor's band was flourishing, and as I said, McKinney's Cotton Pickers were going strong in Detroit.

But at my level and my brother's, the only thing we could do was being unknown teenagers, was to pick up club dates, and a man named Bob Krusett put us in quite a few gigs, local gigs around the area -- Bob Krusett was a saxophone player, and a man named Ben Shipp
Ben Shipp sure. I remember that name.
And we would play for weddings and whatever, you know, whatever the job was -- whether it
was a jazz job or not, you just played -- and sometimes it was a reading of stock orchestrations.
You didn't mention what your brother Gus played, too.

Oh, the trombone. Gus played trombone and piano, but his main instrument was trombone, and arranging -- Gus got into arranging, and was one of the most outstanding of us younger fellows in those days with his arranging.
